name: World Be Free
label: Revelation
lede: Four veterans of Terror, Strife, Judge and Gorilla Biscuits named a band after a basketball player who renamed himself World, then used it to play the melodic, positive hardcore they grew up on.

eras.title: A basketball player's name, four hardcore résumés
eras.text: Scott Vogel of Terror, Andrew Kline of Strife, Joe Garlipp of Despair and Sammy Siegler of Judge start a band that sounds more melodic and more hopeful than any of their others. The name comes off an NBA roster.

years.h: Four bands' worth of members pick a name off an NBA roster
years.p: Lloyd Free changed his first name to World in 1981, and the new band takes it as its own. His line about saying what he'll do and then doing it becomes the motto.
years.xp:
The Idioteq announcement prints the line as Free said it: "I'll say what I'm going to do, and then I'll go out and do it."

Vogel, Kline, Garlipp and Siegler had been in four different hardcore bands. This one was meant to lean toward the melodic, positive records they grew up on.

years.cap: World Be Free at the Union, Los Angeles, February 15, 2016
years.h: Arthur Smilios, Gorilla Biscuits' bassist, fills the last spot
years.p: [[Arthur Smilios|40d4f905-3bb1-4d2e-9a9b-1d7891033094]], who also plays in [[CIV|1649c891-eea0-45b2-8caf-c85d985ff3bd]], takes bass. [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] guests on the song I'm Done.
years.xp: Revelation says Smilios joined after the band formed, while Idioteq's announcement already listed him in late 2015.

eras.title: One drummer, two sets a night
eras.text: The Anti-Circle comes out on Revelation, and the band goes straight on the road, half of it opening for Judge. Sammy Siegler plays drums in both.

years.h: The Anti-Circle lands on Revelation as REV 162
years.p: Cut on a small budget at Hurley Studios on vintage Neve gear. Vogel's vocals were recorded at Nick Jett's studio in Granada Hills.

years.cap: World Be Free at the Union, Los Angeles, February 15, 2016
years.h: San Diego to Brooklyn in nine days, with Judge on the back half
years.p: It opens at San Diego's Che Cafe and a Fullerton skate shop, then Buffalo, Philadelphia and Cambridge opening for Judge. Siegler drums both sets. It ends at St. Vitus in Brooklyn.
years.xp:
Listed dates run February 13 at the Che Cafe, February 14 in Pomona at PBW, February 15 in Los Angeles, February 16 at Programme Skate Shop in Fullerton, then Buffalo's Waiting Room, Philadelphia's Voltage Lounge, Boston's Middle East and St. Vitus on February 21.

hate5six filmed the Philadelphia set on February 19.

eras.title: Four years later, an EP
eras.text: The band goes quiet after the album, loses its bassist to geography, and returns with a Chain of Strength member and a heavier, more melodic EP.

years.h: Smilios stays East; Alex Barreto of Chain of Strength takes bass
years.p: Smilios leaves because his job and life are on the East Coast. [[Alex Barreto|9e81a640-5c20-444e-9064-d2d65cf87328]], also of [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]], takes over.

q: The band was kinda 'dead' for lack of a better term.
years.h: Decibel premieres "Acceptance", the first new song since 2016
years.p: Vogel says hearing Kline's new material is what got him going again. Decibel runs it October 7.

years.h: One Time for Unity picks five songs out of about fifteen
years.p: [[Chuck Ragan|97417292-3fb0-40ea-8837-5540cfb4de71]] of [[Hot Water Music|c83907ee-8b5a-4547-8f68-96572243ea7f]] sings on the title track. Kline calls Down & Beyond World Be Free gone prog.
years.xp:
Kline wrote the music early in the sessions with 1980s DC hardcore in mind. He says Down & Beyond took several revisions and some of the band wanted to drop it.

Vogel on Ragan: "Two words - Chuck Ragan. Dreams do come true."
